body: Odoo 18 have an error, the view `account_sepa_direct_debit.account_payment_register_form_inherit_account_sepa_direct_debit` (Enterprise) references the field `payment_method_code` from `account.payment.register`. This field is added to the model in the `account_payment` module, which is not among the dependencies of `account_sepa_direct_debit`. This means that if the `account_payment` module is not installed, the installation/update of `account_sepa_direct_debit` will also fail. author: rudrigaum
body:
## 📝 Description

This pull request introduces the first complete feature of the application: the **Home Screen**.

It establishes the full MVVM-C stack for this feature, including the creation of a robust, protocol-oriented network layer to fetch product data from the remote API. The result is a fully wired screen that successfully launches, manages its state (`loading`, `success`, `error`), and retrieves data from the backend.

At this stage, the fetched data is logged to the console, proving the end-to-end data flow is working correctly. The next step will be to render this data in the UI.

## 🚀 Changes

- **Model (`Product.swift`):** The core data model for a product was created.
- **Networking Layer (`NetworkService.swift`):** A protocol-oriented `NetworkService` was implemented using modern `async/await` and `URLSession` to fetch an array of `[Product]`. Includes custom error handling.
- **Coordinator (`HomeCoordinator.swift`):** A dedicated coordinator for the Home flow was created and is now initiated by the `AppCoordinator`.
- **View (`HomeView.swift`):** A custom `UIView` subclass was built following the "Owned View" pattern. It contains the `UICollectionView` that will display the products.
- **ViewModel (`HomeViewModel.swift`):** The "brain" of the screen. It uses a `State` enum for state management, fetches data via the injected `NetworkService`, and communicates updates to the `ViewController` via the `HomeViewModelDelegate` pattern to prevent retain cycles.
- **ViewController (`HomeViewController.swift`):** The `ViewController` was updated to be initialized with the `ViewModel` (Dependency Injection). It conforms to the delegate protocol to listen for state changes and triggers the initial data fetch in `viewDidLoad`.

## ✅ How to Test

1.  Check out this branch (`feat/home-screen`).
2.  Build and run the application (`Cmd + R`).
3.  **Expected Result:**
    * The app launches and displays a screen with the navigation bar title "Shopflow".
    * Open the debug console in Xcode.
    * You should see the state changes being printed in order:
      1. `State -> Loading...`
      2. `State -> Success: Received 20 products!` (or the current number from the API).
    * This confirms the entire MVVM-C data flow is correctly implemented.

## ⏭️ Next Steps

- With the data flow now functional, the next PR will focus on the UI rendering:
  - Create a custom `UICollectionViewCell` to display product information.
  - Make the `HomeViewController` conform to `UICollectionViewDataSource`.
  - Populate the collection view with the data received in the `.success` state.

# 🎩 Magic Question

Live Link - https://magic-question-ayushfand.netlify.app

A simple and fun interactive webpage where users choose between three playful options — with audio and animations triggered on hover.
This project is built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and is aimed at learning how to integrate audio into web projects.

# 🚀 Features
🖱️ Interactive Buttons — Each option reacts when hovered.
🔊 Sound Effects — Different audio plays depending on which button is hovered.
🌀 Animation Effects — Buttons shake and text changes dynamically.
🧠 Beginner-Friendly — Simple structure, perfect for early-stage web development learning.

# 🧰 Tech Stack
HTML5 – Structure of the webpage
CSS3 – Styling and animations
JavaScript (Vanilla) – Logic and interactivity
Audio Files (.wav) for sound effects

# 📂 Project Structure
Magic-Question/
│
├── index.html         # Main HTML file
├── fun.css            # Styling file
├── fun.js             # JavaScript logic
├── funny.wav          # Audio file for Play and Food buttons
├── sad.wav            # Audio file for Study button
└── README.md          # Project documentation

# 🧭 How It Works

When the user hovers over a button, a message appears and a sound plays.

When the mouse moves away, the original button text and state are restored.

Different buttons trigger different audio effects.

# 🛠️ How to Run

Clone or download the repository.

Open the index.html file in any browser.

Make sure the audio files (funny.wav and sad.wav) are in the same folder.

Hover over the buttons and enjoy the interaction!

Make the UI more visually appealing with gradients and transitions.

* Applied similar simplification to the changepoint range validation in `model.rs`, using Rust's range syntax for clarity.

**Code Style and Linting:**

* Added `#[allow(dead_code)]` and `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` attributes in several places (including struct fields and function definitions) to suppress warnings from the Rust compiler and Clippy linter, especially for PyO3 and argument-heavy functions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-696ce0c317a2db4770598321bebbe3933696613a3056dbb4e2da5e8f6d0c1f95R92) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8d373c6c7557f71d1072aad7130d0d4b670db6389fe27d46fc9872951d2550e5R10) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-8d373c6c7557f71d1072aad7130d0d4b670db6389fe27d46fc9872951d2550e5R55) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-8d373c6c7557f71d1072aad7130d0d4b670db6389fe27d46fc9872951d2550e5R88) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-8d373c6c7557f71d1072aad7130d0d4b670db6389fe27d46fc9872951d2550e5R122) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-b1a35a68f14e696205874893c07fd24fdb88882b47c23cc0e0c80a30c7d53759R88)
* Added a crate-level allowance for `clippy::useless_conversion` in `lib.rs` to prevent false positives related to PyO3 bindings.

**Minor Logic and Readability Improvements:**

* Refactored candidate path and possible path definitions to use array literals instead of `vec![]` for improved readability and slight performance benefit. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3db3807bf1286f80a3a52f969e11ead8bfe5e65f4b49b51270c251b50eb90c0dL109-R109) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8d373c6c7557f71d1072aad7130d0d4b670db6389fe27d46fc9872951d2550e5L22-R23)
* Simplified logic in the beta extraction loop in `cmdstan_optimizer.rs` by combining conditionals, making the code easier to follow.
* Used direct function reference (`and_then(parse_ds)`) for parsing date strings in model deserialization for conciseness.

Multiple definition sentences begin with a lowercase article/pronoun (e.g., lines 9, 13, 17, 21, 29, 37, 41). Minimal fix: capitalize the first letter of each sentence (e.g., “a free…” → “A free…”). This follows standard English grammar for sentence casing.

Rule: General English grammar (basic rule; the style guide assumes correct sentence mechanics)

**⭐ Favorite flag** - Mark templates as favorites with `is_favorite` boolean field - **🔒 Private flag** - Keep templates private with `is_private` boolean field - Both flags are properly saved to the database and enforced via RLS policies ### Database Schema Created `templates` table with: ```sql - id (UUID Primary Key) - title (TEXT, required) - content (TEXT, required) - is_favorite (BOOLEAN, default false) - is_private (BOOLEAN, default false) - created_by (UUID, references auth.users) - created_at, updated_at (TIMESTAMPTZ) ``` Includes comprehensive Row-Level Security (RLS) policies: - Users can view their own templates and public templates - Users can only create, update, and delete their own templates - Private templates are only visible to their creators ### AI Template Generation - **Supabase Edge Function** at `/generate-template` endpoint - Powered by OpenAI GPT-4o-mini for intelligent template generation - Generates HTML templates based on title input - Includes retry logic, timeout handling, and error recovery - Creates structured templates with placeholders for easy customization ### PDF Export - Client-side PDF generation using `html2pdf.js` - Exports templates with proper formatting and styling - Configurable output options for print quality ### User Experience - Modern UI using Shadcn/ui components - Loading states with animated spinners - Toast notifications for user feedback - Icon indicators (Star for favorite, Lock for private) - Responsive layout and clean design ## Technical Details ### Files Created - author: copilot
body:
## Problem

Highlights were appearing outside or offset from the selected text. When users selected text and saved a highlight, the colored overlay would be drawn at an incorrect position, making the feature unusable.

## Root Cause

The coordinate transformation was using the Stack widget's position as the reference point, but the PDF viewer widget (SfPdfViewer) may have padding, margins, or other layout offsets within the Stack. This caused a mismatch:

- `globalSelectedRegion` returns coordinates in **screen space** (relative to device screen)
- The highlight overlay paints in **widget-local space** (relative to the CustomPaint canvas)
- Transforming relative to the Stack widget didn't account for the PDF viewer's actual position

**Example of the issue:**
```dart
// User selects text at screen position (150, 300)
// Stack is at screen position (0, 56)
// PDF Viewer is at screen position (8, 64) - has 8px padding!

// Old transformation:
localCoords = (150, 300) - (0, 56) = (150, 244)
// Highlight painted at (150, 244), but should be at (142, 236)
// Result: 8px offset ❌
```

## Solution

Changed the coordinate transformation in `_globalToLocal()` to use the PDF viewer widget's position as the reference point:

```dart
// NEW: Use PDF Viewer position (accurate)
final RenderBox? pdfRenderBox = _pdfViewerKey.currentContext?.findRenderObject() as RenderBox?;
if (pdfRenderBox != null) {
  final pdfGlobalPosition = pdfRenderBox.localToGlobal(Offset.zero);
  final localRect = Rect.fromLTRB(
    globalRect.left - pdfGlobalPosition.dx,
    globalRect.top - pdfGlobalPosition.dy,
    globalRect.right - pdfGlobalPosition.dx,
    globalRect.bottom - pdfGlobalPosition.dy,
  );
  return localRect;
}
```

This ensures perfect alignment between where text is selected and where highlights are painted.

## Additional Improvements

### 1. Bounds Validation
Added validation to prevent saving invalid highlights:
- Rejects zero or empty bounds
- Detects out-of-range coordinates (< -1000 or > 10000)
- Provides clear user feedback via snackbars

### 2. Fallback Handling
Implemented a proper fallback chain:
1. Try PDF viewer's RenderBox (most accurate)
2. Fall back to Stack's RenderBox (acceptable)
3. Return `Rect.zero` to trigger validation (instead of wrong coordinates)

### 3. Debug Features (for testing)
- Comprehensive debug logging throughout the coordinate transformation pipeline
- Visual test rectangle (red square at top-left) to verify coordinate system
- Detailed console output for troubleshooting

## Testing

The fix includes several built-in verification features:

**Visual Test**: A small red semi-transparent square appears at position (10, 10) in the PDF viewer. This confirms the coordinate system is working correctly.

**Console Logs**: Debug statements track the transformation at every step:
```
DEBUG: Input globalRect: Rect.fromLTRB(150.0, 300.0, 400.0, 320.0)
DEBUG: PDF Viewer global position: Offset(0.0, 56.0)
DEBUG: Transformed localRect (PDF viewer): Rect.fromLTRB(150.0, 244.0, 400.0, 264.0)
```

**Validation Messages**: Clear snackbar feedback when highlights are saved or if there are issues.

## Expected Behavior After Fix

- ✅ Highlights appear **exactly** over selected text (no offset)
- ✅ Works consistently across all pages
- ✅ Works with all colors (yellow, green, blue, orange, pink, purple)
- ✅ Invalid coordinates are rejected with clear feedback
- ✅ Visual test square confirms coordinate system is functioning

## Documentation

Added comprehensive documentation:
- **HIGHLIGHT_FIX_README.md** - Complete overview and quick start
- **HIGHLIGHT_COORDINATE_FIX_2024.md** - Technical details
- **VISUAL_FIX_EXPLANATION.md** - Visual diagrams showing the fix
- **TESTING_GUIDE_HIGHLIGHTS.md** - Comprehensive testing instructions
- **FIX_SUMMARY.md** - Summary and next steps
- **COORDINATE_FIX_COMPLETE.md** - Quick reference

## Cleanup Note

The debug logging and test rectangle are intentionally included for testing purposes. Once verified working, they can be removed in a follow-up cleanup commit (~30 lines to remove).

## Files Changed

- `lib/main.dart`: Modified coordinate transformation, validation, and painter (+96, -18 lines)
- Added 6 documentation files (1,200+ lines of documentation)

## Backwards Compatibility

- ✅ No breaking changes to API
- ✅ Existing highlights will load (though old coordinates may be wrong)
- ✅ Users should delete old highlights and create new ones after this fix

## Risk Assessment

**Risk Level**: 🟢 Low
- Changes are isolated to highlight functionality
- Easy to rollback if needed
- Backwards compatible
- Includes validation to prevent bad data

**Confidence**: 🟢 High
- Correct solution for coordinate transformation issues
- Includes verification features
- Comprehensive documentation

body:
This pull request introduces several improvements to the application's configuration management, UI responsiveness, and user experience, especially around theme selection and scan feedback. The most notable changes include persisting configuration updates to disk, enhancing the Home screen with theme selection and notification features, and providing clearer feedback during scan operations.

### Configuration persistence and validation

* Updates to `ConfigLoader` methods now ensure that changes to splash screen, theme, and license key settings are immediately written to disk, improving reliability of configuration changes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-135b086749b25117aa7459b78750c32a547be8de2966d7e9df44c8ba21684c92R5) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-135b086749b25117aa7459b78750c32a547be8de2966d7e9df44c8ba21684c92L210-R214) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-135b086749b25117aa7459b78750c32a547be8de2966d7e9df44c8ba21684c92L228-R234) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-135b086749b25117aa7459b78750c32a547be8de2966d7e9df44c8ba21684c92R250-R254)
* The theme setter in `AppConfig.java` is now documented to accept values between 1 and 4 (previously 0–4), clarifying valid input.

### Home screen UI enhancements

* The Home screen now includes a theme picker combo box, allowing users to select and persist their preferred UI theme; the picker is initialized and rendered with user-friendly names, and updates are saved to config.
* Notification panels and tooltips for monitored directories have been added, providing visual cues about baseline status and scan recency.

### Improved scan handling and feedback

* Scan operations now distinguish baseline scans and provide specific success messages; the live feed is updated to indicate when a baseline is being established. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b2f87dc17460a58dc8c93ffd1475ced525268bbe6ccc4bc74c46b464c770cff8R474-R508) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b2f87dc17460a58dc8c93ffd1475ced525268bbe6ccc4bc74c46b464c770cff8R632-R649)
* On scan completion, the dialog message now reflects whether a baseline scan was performed, improving clarity for the user.

### General UI/UX improvements

* Table and list selection models are set to single selection for better usability and consistency across views.
* The Home screen's refresh logic is updated to show notifications and set up list renderers for monitored directories.

### Minor fixes

* The login screen now clears username and password fields when shown, ensuring a clean state for new logins.

https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/ecosystem/blueprint/benchmarks.mdx?plain=1#L25-L26

“we’ve introduced a reporting system that lets you collect and compare metrics…” uses ambiguous “we.” Prefer direct instructions or neutral phrasing. Minimal fix: “A reporting system lets you collect and compare metrics across versions.” or “Use the reporting system to collect and compare metrics across versions.”
Rule: https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/contribute/style-guide-extended.mdx?plain=1#voice-and-tone

---

- [ ] **2. “Note:” label styled with bold instead of an Aside**

https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/ecosystem/blueprint/benchmarks.mdx?plain=1#L45-L49

“**Note:**” with a bullet list simulates a callout using bold. Render callouts with the `<Aside>` component. Minimal fix: wrap the bullets in `<Aside type="note">…</Aside>` and drop the bold label.
Rule: https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/contribute/style-guide-extended.mdx?plain=1#a-admonition-levels-and-usage

---

- [ ] **3. Headings must not contain code formatting**

https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/ecosystem/blueprint/benchmarks.mdx?plain=1#L279-L303

The H4 headings include backticked filenames: “`jest.config.ts`” and “`gas-report.config.ts`”. Headings must not contain code styling. Minimal fix: remove backticks in headings: “Option 1: update the existing jest.config.ts” and “Option 2: create a separate config gas-report.config.ts”. Keep code styling for these filenames in body text as needed.
Rule: https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/contribute/style-guide-extended.mdx?plain=1#headings-and-titles

---

- [ ] **4. Product name capitalization and unnecessary bolding (“jest”)**

https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/ecosystem/blueprint/benchmarks.mdx?plain=1#L276

“configure **jest** to collect gas metrics.” uses lowercase and bold for the product name. Capitalize proper nouns and avoid decorative bolding. Minimal fix: “configure Jest to collect gas metrics.”
Rule: https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/contribute/style-guide-extended.mdx?plain=1#general-casing-rules

---

- [ ] **5. Token styled in bold instead of code font**

https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/ecosystem/blueprint/benchmarks.mdx?plain=1#L170

The opcode name is styled as **increase**. Use code font for identifiers. Minimal fix: change to `increase`.
Rule: https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/contribute/style-guide-extended.mdx?plain=1#code-styling

---

- [ ] **6. Acronym not expanded on first use (“ABI”)**

https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/ecosystem/blueprint/benchmarks.mdx?plain=1#L30

Spell out on first mention. Minimal fix: “Application Binary Interface (ABI) information from the snapshot …”. This uses general English/industry knowledge of the acronym.
Rule: https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/contribute/style-guide-extended.mdx?plain=1#acronyms-and-terms

---

- [ ] **7. Task heading should be imperative**

https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/ecosystem/blueprint/benchmarks.mdx?plain=1#L274

“Project setup instructions” is a noun phrase. For procedure sections, start headings with an imperative verb. Minimal fix: “Set up the project” or “Configure Jest for gas metrics”.
Rule: https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/contribute/style-guide-extended.mdx?plain=1#headings-and-titles

---

- [ ] **8. Use stable permalinks instead of ‘main’ for deep links**

https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/ecosystem/blueprint/benchmarks.mdx?plain=1#L30-L359

Deep links to GitHub use the moving `main` branch (e.g., `https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/.../blob/main/docs/collect-metric-api.md?plain=1#...`). For precision-critical references, link to a versioned permalink (tag or commit). Minimal fix: replace `/blob/main/` with a specific tag or commit permalink in each URL. Domain owner must choose the appropriate version/tag.
Rule: https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/contribute/style-guide-extended.mdx?plain=1#stable-permalinks-situation-aware

---

- [ ] **9. Minor grammar in code comment (“if need”)**

https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/ecosystem/blueprint/benchmarks.mdx?plain=1#L310-L311

The comment reads “use filter tests if need, see …”. Prefer standard phrasing. Minimal fix: “Filter tests if needed; see https://jestjs.io/docs/cli#--testnamepatternregex”. This fix relies on general English grammar.
Rule: https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/contribute/style-guide-extended.mdx?plain=1#grammar-and-usage

---

- [ ] **10. Callout severity: use Note instead of Tip**

https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/ecosystem/blueprint/benchmarks.mdx?plain=1#L15-L21

The callout provides auxiliary references, not actionable productivity tips. Use the least severe level; map to `type="note"`. Minimal fix: change `<Aside type="tip">` to `<Aside type="note">`.
Rule: https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/contribute/style-guide-extended.mdx?plain=1#a-admonition-levels-and-usage

---

- [ ] **11. Link text not descriptive/mismatched with target**

https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/ecosystem/blueprint/benchmarks.mdx?plain=1#L165

Link text “calculator example” points to `/ton/phases-and-fees`, whose page title is “Execution phases and fees” and currently has no “calculator example” section. Make link text descriptive and aligned with the target. Minimal fix: change link text to “Execution phases and fees”.
Rule: https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/contribute/style-guide-extended.mdx?plain=1#link-text

---

- [ ] **12. Broken internal link anchor (inline specifier)**

https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/ecosystem/blueprint/benchmarks.mdx?plain=1#L228

The link points to an anchor that does not exist: [/language/func/functions#inline-specifier]. Anchors must resolve. Minimal fix: link to the page without a nonexistent anchor ("/language/func/functions") or update to the correct existing anchor once confirmed by the domain owner.
Rule: https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/contribute/style-guide-extended.mdx?plain=1#12-3-link-targets-and-format

---

- [ ] **13. Passive voice; rewrite to active**

https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/ecosystem/blueprint/benchmarks.mdx?plain=1#L30-L32

"Before running the tests, a store is created... After test execution, the collected metrics are supplemented..., and a report is generated." Use active voice. author: glower
body:
This commit overhauls the core document processing system to make it faster, more scalable, and more effective.

- **Faster Indexing:** Repository loading is now a concurrent pipeline that uses multiple CPU cores to process files in parallel.
- **Handles Large Repos:** The system now uses a fixed amount of memory and can index repositories of any size without crashing.
- **Better AI Context:** The Go chunking logic has been improved to create larger, more meaningful chunks of code. This gives the AI better context, leading to higher-quality analysis and answers.
- **Increased Stability:** The Ollama client has been hardened to prevent race conditions and potential deadlocks during operation

author: gusarich
body:
- [ ] **1. Use present tense instead of future ("will …")**

https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/language/func/compiler-directives.mdx?plain=1#L21

Several sentences use future tense for general behavior (e.g., “the compiler will ignore…”, “A warning will be issued…”, “will be evaluated…”, “will contain…”). Use present tense for general behavior and instructions. Minimal fixes: “By default, the compiler ignores redundant inclusions… A warning is issued if the verbosity level is 2 or higher.” Likewise: “is evaluated in the following order”, “contains…”.
Rule: https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/contribute/style-guide-extended.mdx?plain=1#5-1-voice-tense-and-person

---

- [ ] **2. Avoid passive voice when the actor is known**

https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/language/func/compiler-directives.mdx?plain=1#L21

“Files are automatically checked for multiple inclusions.” Use active voice with the actor: “The compiler automatically checks files for multiple inclusions.”
Rule: https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/contribute/style-guide-extended.mdx?plain=1#5-1-voice-tense-and-person

---

- [ ] **3. Code tokens and patterns styled as italics; use code font**

https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/language/func/compiler-directives.mdx?plain=1#L33

Operators and version patterns appear in italics (e.g., “_a.b.c_”, “_=_”, “_>_”, “_>=_”, “_\<_”, “_\<=_”). Render tokens and literals in code font. Minimal fix: use code spans for operators and patterns: `a.b.c`, `=a.b.c`, `>a.b.c`, `>=a.b.c`, `<a.b.c`, `<=a.b.c`, `^a.b`, `^a`. Remove backslash escapes once in code font.
Rule: https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/contribute/style-guide-extended.mdx?plain=1#6-3-code-styling

---

- [ ] **4. Malformed emphasis and grammar in caret (“^”) examples**

https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/language/func/compiler-directives.mdx?plain=1#L49

Text reads: “_^a.b_—Requires the major compiler version to be \*_equal_ to _a_ part and minor be **no lower** than _b_ part;”. Fix broken Markdown and grammar, avoid bold for emphasis, and use code font for `a`/`b`. Minimal fix: “`^a.b`—Requires the major compiler version to be equal to the `a` part, and the minor is no lower than the `b` part.”
Rule: https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/contribute/style-guide-extended.mdx?plain=1#6-3-code-styling; https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/contribute/style-guide-extended.mdx?plain=1#6-2-quotation-marks-and-emphasis

---

- [ ] **5. List item punctuation: use periods for full sentences**

https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/language/func/compiler-directives.mdx?plain=1#L43

Items under “Supported comparison operators” end with semicolons though they read as full sentences. End full-sentence list items with periods (or make them fragments and omit terminal punctuation consistently). Minimal fix: change trailing semicolons to periods in items at 43–50, and in example bullets at 55–57 and 61–62.
Rule: https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/contribute/style-guide-extended.mdx?plain=1#6-4-lists

---

- [ ] **6. Extra spacing and punctuation inside code tokens**

https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/language/func/compiler-directives.mdx?plain=1#L52

There is an extra space before a comma and terminal punctuation appears inside tokens (e.g., “`a.b.0.`”). Do not add punctuation inside code that isn’t part of the literal, and avoid stray spaces. Minimal fix: remove the space before the comma in “`(_=_, _>_, _>=_, _\<_, _\<=_), omitted`” and move periods outside code spans (e.g., “`a.b.0`.”).
Rule: https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/contribute/style-guide-extended.mdx?plain=1#6-3-code-styling

---

- [ ] **7. Ordered lists should use `1.` auto-numbering**

https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/language/func/compiler-directives.mdx?plain=1#L118

Numbered sequences use explicit 1., 2., 3., 4. Each ordered list item should start with `1.` and let the renderer auto-number. Minimal fix: change the items at 118–121 and 141–144 to start with `1.`.
Rule: https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/contribute/style-guide-extended.mdx?plain=1#6-4-lists

---

- [ ] **8. Bold labels used as pseudo-headings; use real headings**

https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/language/func/compiler-directives.mdx?plain=1#L15

“**Syntax:**” is a bolded label. Do not use bold for structure. Minimal fix: make it a heading `#### Syntax`.
Rule: https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/contribute/style-guide-extended.mdx?plain=1#6-2-quotation-marks-and-emphasis; https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/contribute/style-guide-extended.mdx?plain=1#7-headings-and-titles

---

- [ ] **9. Unlabeled partial snippet with ellipsis; label as Not runnable**

https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/language/func/compiler-directives.mdx?plain=1#L133

The code block includes `...`, indicating omitted context, but lacks a “Not runnable” label. Partial snippets must be labeled. Minimal fix: add a line “Not runnable” immediately above the fenced block per §10.2.
Rule: https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/contribute/style-guide-extended.mdx?plain=1#10-2-partial-snippets

---

- [ ] **10. Note styled as bold text; use an Aside callout**

https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/language/func/compiler-directives.mdx?plain=1#L150

The line starts with “**Note:**” to call out scope. Use the `<Aside>` component for callouts. Minimal fix: replace with `<Aside type="note"> `#pragma compute-asm-ltr` applies only to code after the directive in the file. </Aside>`.
Rule: https://github.com/tact-lang/mintlify-ton-docs/blob/53b6c23461988d04871b01bac537f21fbd21f860/contribute/style-guide-extended.mdx?plain=1#a-admonition-levels-and-usage

---

We've had recurring issues with PRs' `CHANGELOG.md` entries going stale, particularly when PRs are filed close to a regular release date. This PR tries to make this by creating a CI check that fails when a PR modifies the changelog and it detects changes outside the `## Unreleased` section header.

body:
## Overview

Implements a new Supabase Edge Function for rewriting text snippets with clear, formal, and technical maritime language. This API is optimized for operational templates, checklists, and technical documentation.

## What's New

### Supabase Edge Function: `rewrite-template`

A specialized text rewriting API that uses GPT-4 with a maritime technical assistant persona to transform casual text into formal operational language.

**Endpoint**: `POST /functions/v1/rewrite-template`

**Example Request**:
```json
{
  "input": "O capitão deve verificar os equipamentos antes de sair"
}
```

**Example Response**:
```json
{
  "result": "O comandante deve realizar inspeção completa de todos os equipamentos antes da partida.",
  "timestamp": "2025-10-14T19:47:26.102Z"
}
```

## Key Features

- **GPT-4 Model**: Higher quality output for precise technical rewriting
- **Temperature 0.4**: Produces formal, consistent, and professional results
- **Maritime Technical Focus**: Specialized prompt for operational templates
- **Robust Error Handling**: 3 retry attempts with exponential backoff
- **Timeout Protection**: 30-second request timeout
- **CORS Enabled**: Ready for cross-origin requests

## Technical Implementation

The function implements:
- Input validation and error handling
- Retry logic with exponential backoff (1s → 2s → 4s) for network resilience
- Proper error logging with `[REWRITE_TEMPLATE_ERROR]` tag
- Comprehensive timeout protection using AbortController
- Full CORS support for frontend integration

## Comparison with `rewrite-document`

| Feature | rewrite-template (NEW) | rewrite-document |
|---------|------------------------|------------------|
| **Purpose** | Short text snippets | Full documents |
| **Model** | GPT-4 | GPT-4o-mini |
| **Temperature** | 0.4 (formal) | 0.7 (creative) |
| **Focus** | Maritime technical | General professional |
| **Use Case** | Templates, checklists | Documents, reports |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { supabase } from "@/integrations/supabase/client";

async function rewriteTemplate(input: string) {
  const { data, error } = await supabase.functions.invoke("rewrite-template", {
    body: { input },
  });

  if (error) {
    console.error("Error:", error);
    return null;
  }

  return data.result;
}

// Transform casual text into formal maritime language
const result = await rewriteTemplate("O capitão deve verificar os equipamentos");
// Returns: "O comandante deve realizar inspeção dos equipamentos"
```

## Use Cases

1. **Operational Templates**: Standardize procedures with formal technical language
2. **Checklist Items**: Refine checklist descriptions for clarity
3. **Maritime Communications**: Formalize ship-to-shore communications
4. **Training Materials**: Improve instructional content quality
5. **Technical Documentation**: Enhance equipment and procedure descriptions

## Configuration

Requires `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variable to be set in Supabase Edge Functions configuration.

## Documentation

Complete documentation provided in:
- `supabase/functions/rewrite-template/README.md` - Full API reference
- `REWRITE_TEMPLATE_API_IMPLEMENTATION.md` - Implementation details
- `REWRITE_TEMPLATE_QUICKREF.md` - Quick start guide
- `REWRITE_TEMPLATE_VISUAL_SUMMARY.md` - Executive summary

## Testing

- ✅ Build passes (44.29s)
- ✅ All 262 tests pass
- ✅ No linting errors
- ✅ Follows existing codebase patterns

## Deployment

Ready to deploy with:
```bash
supabase functions deploy rewrite-template
```

---

This implementation provides a refined, GPT-4-powered solution for rewriting text with formal maritime technical language, perfectly suited for operational templates and technical documentation in the Travel HR Buddy maritime system.

author: googlyrahman
body:
Automated: Migrate paths from gsutil to gcloud storage

This CL is part of the on going effort to migrate from the legacy `gsutil` tool to the new and improved `gcloud storage` command-line interface. `gcloud storage` is the recommended and modern tool for interacting with Google Cloud Storage, offering better performance, unified authentication, and a more consistent command structure with other `gcloud` components. 🚀

### Automation Details

This change was **generated automatically** by an agent that targets users of `gsutil`.
The transformations applied are based on the  [gsutil to gcloud storage migration guide](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/gsutil/blob/master/GCLOUD-MIGRATION.md).

### ⚠️ Action Required: Please Review and Test Carefully

While we have based the automation on the migration guide, every use case is unique.
**It is crucial that you thoroughly test these changes in environments appropriate to your use-case before merging.**
Be aware of potential differences between `gsutil` and `gcloud storage` that could impact your workflows.
For instance, the structure of command output may have changed, requiring updates to any scripts that parse it. Similarly, command behavior can differ subtly; the `gcloud storage rsync` command has a different file deletion logic than `gsutil rsync`, which could lead to unintended file deletions.

Our migration guides can help guide you through a list of mappings and some notable differences between the two tools.

Standard presubmit tests are run as part of this CL's workflow. **If you need to target an additional test workflow or require assistance with testing, please let us know.**

Please verify that all your Cloud Storage operations continue to work as expected to avoid any potential disruptions in production.

### Support and Collaboration

The `GCS CLI` team is here to help! If you encounter any issues, have a complex use case that this automated change doesn't cover, or face any other blockers, please don't hesitate to reach out.
We are happy to work with you to test and adjust these changes as needed.

**Contact:** `gcs-cli-hyd@google.com`

We appreciate your partnership in this important migration effort!

If you have a local https / squid proxy, you can speed up your local ublue image builds by orders of magnitude by simply setting some variables and mounting the correct files. This can be a bit confusing and complex for new users.

This PR introduce a proxy-cert helper to capture proxy CA and a shared podman-proxy-flags.sh script so every podman build/run inherits proxy settings and mounts the captured certificate.

Note, this only happens if you have set https_proxy variable set. There is a message to suggest you run `just proxy-cert` or manually copy in cache/https-proxy-ca.pem if it doesn't already exist.

author: kobzol
body:
While testing the new system on the x64 collector, I ran into some panics caused by missing API keys that I did not configure. I realized that in the case of panic, the cron job would stop, but the website would happily chug along. That's not really ideal.

The rustc-perf codebase uses unwraps and panics on a bunch of places, and thus panics can sometime happen, e.g. from transient network or DB errors. This PR thus pre-emptively guards against the panics by restarting the job queue handler cron job when it panics.

Special care is taken to avoid a "panic loop", where we would restart the task and it would immediately panic again.

author: mtwichel
body:
## Summary

This PR implements a sophisticated metadata storage system with image deduplication based on original filenames.

## Key Features

- **Hive-backed metadata store** for persistent metadata storage
- **O(1) deduplication** by original filename - when you upload the same filename, it updates the existing file instead of creating a new one
- **Simplified approach** - no content hashing needed, just filename-based deduplication
- **Backward compatible** - maintains legacy .meta files

## Implementation Details

### Architecture
- Single Hive box with O(1) lookups keyed by `originalName`
- Stores: originalName, secureFileName, uploadedAt, fileSize
- When uploading a file with an existing filename, updates the file and metadata with new timestamp

### Behavior
```bash
# First upload of photo.jpg
→ Creates: 1234567890_123456.jpg
→ Returns: /files/1234567890_123456.jpg

# Re-upload photo.jpg (any content)
→ Updates: 1234567890_123456.jpg  (same file!)
→ Returns: /files/1234567890_123456.jpg  (same URL!)

# Upload different_photo.jpg
→ Creates: 9876543210_654321.jpg  (new file)
→ Returns: /files/9876543210_654321.jpg  (new URL)
```

## Files Changed

- `lib/src/metadata.dart` - New metadata model and store
- `lib/src/image_upload_utils.dart` - Updated upload logic with deduplication
- `main.dart` - Initialize metadata store
- `routes/_middleware.dart` - Provide metadata store in context
- `routes/upload_tokens/[token].dart` - Use metadata store during upload
- `routes/files/index.dart` - Use metadata store during upload
- `pubspec.yaml` - Dependencies (no crypto needed)

## Testing

- ✅ 11 tests passing
- ✅ Metadata store CRUD operations
- ✅ Deduplication logic
- ✅ Filename-based updates
- ✅ No analyzer errors

## Performance

- O(1) lookup for duplicate detection
- Single box instead of complex multi-box architecture
- No hashing overhead on uploads
- Clean, maintainable code

### Description
- **Summary**: Replace passive cleanup with explicit handling of finished tasks. When a blob task finishes, we remove it from the map, await its JoinHandle, and log any error.
- **Problem**: Previously, JoinHandle results were discarded; task errors were silently lost and concurrency counters risked sticking on failure.
- **Change**: In `crates/full-node/sov-blob-sender/src/lib.rs`, replace `retain`-based cleanup with:

  - Remove them under lock
  - Await their handles
  - Log errors if any

author: danval-003
body:
This pull request introduces new functionality for handling "dataset" fields in forms, allowing users to retrieve datasets as tables both globally and for specific forms. It adds new API endpoints to expose this data, and implements the backend logic to efficiently query and normalize datasets from different schema versions. The changes also include new TypeScript types to structure the dataset table responses.

**New API endpoints for datasets**  
- Added `GET /forms/datasets` to retrieve all datasets visible to the user, and `GET /forms/:id/datasets` to retrieve datasets for a specific form, with optional 404 response when no datasets are found.
- Added `POST /forms/entries` endpoint for creating form entries.

**Backend logic for dataset tables**  
- Implemented `getUserDatasetsAsTables` method in `FormsService` to aggregate and normalize dataset fields into tables, supporting both legacy and new database schemas. This method handles visibility, schema detection, and data normalization.

**TypeScript types for dataset tables**  
- Introduced `DatasetTable` and `DatasetTableRow` types to strongly type the structure of dataset tables and their rows.

**Controller improvements and imports**  
- Updated `FormsController` to use new endpoints and cleaned up imports, adding missing decorators and HTTP method imports.

**Minor improvements**  
- Clarified comments to indicate that the tree endpoint groups forms by category, not hierarchy.

author: matthew-bass
body:
I added a way to download the HIBP database as a single, sorted file (`--combine`) and a way to only download the "diff" of what I had already downloaded using eTags (`--sync`).

### `--combine`

To implement this, I made a `HashWriter` trait, and then had `IndividualWriter` / `CombinedWriter` as the implementations. When downloading the hashes the downloader function gets passed the respective writer.

Since I wanted to have the output file sorted, and the hash ranges are downloaded in parallel I had the combined writer store a buffer of etags so it can write sequentially to the file as the "next range block" becomes available.

The combined writer prepends the hash prefix for each file (so it now stores the full 40-character sha1) because you can't infer the 5 digit k-anon prefix from the filename in this model.

### `--sync`

I wanted a way to only grab the changes to the HIBP since the last time I had downloaded the data. I felt the easiest way to get something similar was to use the eTags in a similar manner to how `--resume` worked. The `--sync` command accepts an etag cache, which I use as a smaller representation of the downloaded database.

If `--sync` is passed, I look up if the etag is the same in the etag cache and skip the range if needed similar to resume.

You can use `--sync` along with `--resume`, and it'll still respect both.

Using the sync cache now "downloads" the entire database in a couple (i.e. 2) minutes, as opposed to the 10-20 if doing the full download.

`test_etag_sync.sh` is a script I used to verify that the etag cache accurately matches what the actual downloaded state is if the process is killed. So, there's no extra etags in the cache for data that wasn't downloaded, or data that was downloaded was missing entries in the sync cache.

author: incertum
body:
Deprecates all metric creation methods that accept loose string parameters for name and help text.

This standardizes metric creation on the MetricNameDescriptor type, which requires a metricName, unitName and helpText for all metrics. This improves compliance with official Prometheus client library guidelines ("A MetricFamily MUST have a name, HELP, TYPE, and UNIT metadata.").

The deprecated methods will be removed in a future major version (see https://github.com/swift-server/swift-prometheus/issues/145).

CC @ktoso, thank you!

author: wodann
body:
Since the Spurious Dragon hardfork, accounts are considered empty if the code is empty, balance is zero, and nonce is zero.
Before the Spurious Dragon hardfork, there was a distinction between "existing" and "empty" states.

REVM's codebase models this behaviour [here](https://github.com/bluealloy/revm/blob/main/crates/state/src/lib.rs#L63).

Remote providers, like Alchemy & Infura, return empty account information when querying for non-existing accounts. This breaks the `Journal` logic that would previously set the `status` flags to mark an account as "not existing" [here](https://github.com/bluealloy/revm/blob/main/crates/context/src/journal/inner.rs#L732).

As a result, [this line](https://github.com/bluealloy/revm/blob/main/crates/handler/src/pre_execution.rs#L225) caused the EIP-7702 gas cost refunds to be calculated incorrectly. I added a test that demonstrates this failure.

Since EIP-7702 was introduced after the Spurious Dragon hardfork, the existing logic to check for pre-Spurious dragon non-existing accounts was not necessary at all. Thus I was able to fix the issue by not checking for both conditions.

Since our team is still using REVM v83, I would also like to fix that release v83 and publish a new release. I don't seem to be able to create a PR for that tag. Could you please help me with that?

This is the comparison of our v83 branch with the tag: https://github.com/bluealloy/revm/compare/v83...NomicFoundation:revm:fix/v83-eip7702-refund

There were two bugs affecting the course sync if conditions were such that a course was requested in LSApp, then created in ELM, but LSApp's data isn't updated with the ELM info (`ITEM-NNNN` code) in time before a sync runs.

There are detailed explanations of each bug and what was done to fix them in two files:

- course-feed/duplicate-detection-implementation.md
- course-feed/empty-itemcode-collision-fix.md

So now, we run extra validation to ensure the duplicates are not created and if the situation is detected then we stop processing and send an email to corporate.learning.admin@gov.bc.ca

Additionally, we created an overall sync explanation document in:

course-feed/course-sync-explainer.md

Lastly, there's a tweak in here so that the sync now stops processing any actions after feed-create.php is run, so now the sync process really does just sync ELM with LSApp and then produces the data to sync with LearningHUB and no longer processes open access publishing, or RSS feed creation for anything.

# chore(ci): add permissions to workflow files

## Summary
Added explicit `permissions: contents: read` declarations to GitHub Actions workflow files (`.github/workflows/add-asana-comment.yml` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml`). This follows GitHub's security best practices by explicitly declaring the minimum required permissions for workflows rather than relying on default permissions, implementing the principle of least privilege.

Previously, these workflows inherited the repository's default permissions. By explicitly setting `contents: read`, we ensure these workflows operate with only the access they need - read-only access to repository contents for running CI checks and posting Asana comments.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human
- [ ] **Verify CI checks pass** - Confirm all GitHub Actions workflows complete successfully with the new permissions
- [ ] **Confirm workflows don't require write access** - If any workflow fails due to permission errors, we may need to add specific write permissions for that workflow

body: --- ### What does this PR do? This PR implements a comprehensive fuzzing test suite that automatically discovers security vulnerabilities and edge cases through randomized testing. The framework includes: - **Input Validation Fuzzing**: Tests all contract functions with random, malformed, and extreme inputs to discover input validation vulnerabilities - **Oracle Response Fuzzing**: Simulates malicious oracle responses to test manipulation resistance (price manipulation, confidence attacks, timestamp manipulation) - **Market State Fuzzing**: Validates market state consistency and detects state manipulation vulnerabilities (vote manipulation, invalid resolutions) - **Dispute Mechanism Fuzzing**: Tests dispute scenarios including zero-stake attacks, double disputes, and front-running attempts - **Fee Calculation Fuzzing**: Discovers arithmetic vulnerabilities (overflow/underflow) in fee calculations - **Automated Vulnerability Detection**: Intelligent classification of errors into security vulnerabilities vs. expected failures - **Severity Assessment**: Automatic severity scoring (Critical/High/Medium/Low/Info) for discovered issues The framework runs 1000+ iterations per test category by default, generating edge cases, attack vectors, and random inputs to maximize coverage. ### Why is this change needed? **Critical Security Gap**: We currently have NO fuzzing tests, which means: - No automated discovery of input validation vulnerabilities - No testing against malicious oracle responses - No validation of arithmetic safety (overflow/underflow) - No discovery of state manipulation vulnerabilities - No automated edge case discovery - Vulnerabilities may only be discovered in production (catastrophic risk) Fuzzing is an industry-standard security practice that has discovered critical vulnerabilities in major smart contracts. author: 0xferit
body:
## Summary
Standardizes native ETH representation from the non-standard sentinel `0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE` to the ecosystem-standard `address(0)`, defined as `NATIVE_TOKEN` in `src/constants.sol`.

## Key Changes

### Zero As Initialization Sentinel
- **Fixed initialization bug**: Changed initialization guard from `address(S.asset) != address(0)` to `S.management != address(0)`
  - **Why**: With `address(0)` as native ETH, checking `S.asset` would fail for ETH strategies
  - **Solution**: Use `S.management` which is always non-zero after initialization (enforced on line 746-748)
- **Updated constructor**: Now locks implementation via `S.management = address(1)` instead of `S.asset`

### Refactoring
- **Removed all local constant redeclarations**: Eliminated duplicate `ETH` constants across 20+ files  
- **Centralized constant**: All files now import `NATIVE_TOKEN` from `src/constants.sol`  
- **Updated all references**: Replaced `0xEeeee...` and local `ETH` with `NATIVE_TOKEN` throughout codebase  

## Rationale

1. **Ecosystem Alignment**: 
   - Gnosis Safe uses `address(0)` for ETH
   - 0xSplits library (already in codebase) uses `address(0)` 
   - Industry standard convention

2. **Type Safety**: 
   - `S.asset` is typed as `ERC20` (contract type)
   - Native ETH is not an ERC20
   - Using `address(0)` with proper guards avoids type system abuse

3. **Code Quality**:
   - Single source of truth (`src/constants.sol`)
   - No redundant constant declarations
   - Cleaner, more maintainable code



## Verification
✅ `forge build` succeeds  
✅ No `0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE` references remain  
✅ All constants imported from `src/constants.sol`  
✅ Initialization guard properly prevents re-initialization for ETH strategies

## Overview

This PR implements a complete end-to-end MCP (Model Context Protocol) server using Python, FastAPI, and the official FastMCP SDK. The server integrates with Adobe IMS OAuth to provide a personalized greeting tool that fetches user information from Adobe's UserInfo endpoint and returns a greeting using the user's name.

**MCP Server Implementation:**
- Built with FastAPI and FastMCP SDK
- Implements Streamable HTTP (SSE) transport compatible with ChatGPT's Apps SDK
- Exposes MCP endpoint at `/mcp` for protocol communication

**Adobe OAuth 2.0 Integration:**
- Full Authorization Code Grant flow with Adobe IMS
- Token verification against Adobe IMS before processing requests
- UserInfo API integration to fetch user profile data
- RFC 8414 compliant OAuth metadata endpoint at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`

**MCP Tool: `hello_user`**
- Accepts an OAuth access token as a parameter
- Verifies the token with Adobe IMS
- Fetches user information from Adobe's UserInfo endpoint
- Extracts the user's name from their Adobe profile
- Returns a personalized greeting: "Hello, [Your Name]! 👋"
- Includes comprehensive error handling for invalid or expired tokens

### Architecture

```
┌─────────────┐      OAuth Flow       ┌──────────────┐
│   ChatGPT   │ ◄──────────────────► │  Adobe IMS   │
└──────┬──────┘                       └──────────────┘
       │                                     ▲
       │ MCP Protocol (SSE)                  │
       │                                     │ Token Verification
       ▼                                     │ & UserInfo API
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│     FastAPI + FastMCP Server                │
│  - OAuth Metadata Endpoint                  │
│  - MCP Tools (hello_user)                   │
│  - Health Check                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Files Added

### Core Application (4 files)
- **`server.py`** - Main FastAPI application with FastMCP integration and OAuth service
- **`requirements.txt`** - Python dependencies (FastAPI, FastMCP, httpx, etc.)
- **`.env.example`** - Environment configuration template for Adobe credentials
- **`.gitignore`** - Git ignore patterns for sensitive files and build artifacts

### Documentation (4 files)
- **`README.md`** - Comprehensive documentation with architecture overview, setup instructions, API endpoints, OAuth flow explanation, and troubleshooting guide
- **`QUICKSTART.md`** - Quick start guide for local development and Docker deployment
- **`CHATGPT_INTEGRATION.md`** - Step-by-step guide for integrating the MCP server with ChatGPT
- **`mcp-config.json`** - Example MCP configuration for ChatGPT Apps

### Development Tools (3 files)
- **`test_server.py`** - Server structure validation script
- **`demo.py`** - OAuth flow demonstration script
- **`verify_setup.py`** - Pre-flight setup verification tool

### Deployment (2 files)
- **`Dockerfile`** - Docker image configuration
- **`docker-compose.yml`** - Docker Compose orchestration for easy deployment

## API Endpoints

1. **`GET /health`** - Health check endpoint
2. **`GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`** - OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata (RFC 8414)
3. **`POST/SSE /mcp`** - MCP protocol endpoint with Server-Sent Events transport

## Security Features

- Token verification before processing any requests
- Environment variable-based configuration for sensitive credentials
- `.env` file excluded from version control
- Async HTTP client with appropriate timeouts
- Comprehensive error handling for API failures
- HTTPS recommended for production deployments

## Usage

After setting up Adobe OAuth credentials:

```bash
# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Configure environment
cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env with Adobe credentials

# Verify setup
python verify_setup.py

# Start server
python server.py
```

The server will be available at `http://localhost:8000` with the MCP endpoint at `http://localhost:8000/mcp`.

## Testing

The implementation includes several tools for validation:
- **`verify_setup.py`** - Checks Python version, file presence, environment configuration, and dependencies
- **`test_server.py`** - Validates server structure and component presence
- **`demo.py`** - Demonstrates the OAuth flow and tool usage

## Deployment Options

- **Local development**: Direct Python execution
- **Docker**: Using provided Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml
- **Cloud platforms**: AWS, GCP, Azure, Heroku, Railway, Fly.io, etc.

## Next Steps

Users need to:
1. Obtain Adobe OAuth credentials from [Adobe Developer Console](https://developer.adobe.com/console)
2. Configure their `.env` file with the credentials
3. Install dependencies and start the server
4. Configure ChatGPT to connect to the MCP endpoint
5. Authorize with their Adobe account
6. Use the `hello_user` tool to receive personalized greetings

## References

- [MCP Specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/)
- [FastMCP Documentation](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp)
- [Adobe IMS Documentation](https://developer.adobe.com/developer-console/docs/guides/authentication/)
- [FastAPI Documentation](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/)

> I want an end-to-end setup using Python + FastAPI + the official MCP Python SDK (FastMCP). It supports the Apps SDK “Streamable HTTP” transport, declares OAuth per the MCP auth spec, verifies tokens against Adobe IMS, calls Adobe UserInfo to get your name, and returns a personalized greeting.

## Overview

Enhances the Bazzite Driver Versions Report with better usability for GamersNexus users who need to troubleshoot driver-specific issues by rebasing to specific versions. The report now covers 3 months of stable releases with complete driver information.

## Changes Made

### 1. Added Rebase Command Column
Each release now includes a ready-to-use command for quick rebasing:
```bash
bazzite-rollback-helper rebase 42.20251011
```
This eliminates the need for users to manually construct commands from the documentation.

### 2. Expanded Release Coverage (3 → 8 releases)
Added 5 additional stable releases to provide better historical context:
- 42.20250911 (Sep 11, 2025)
- 42.20250908 (Sep 8, 2025)  
- 42.20250903 (Sep 3, 2025)
- 42.20250901 (Sep 1, 2025)
- 42.20250828.1 (Aug 28, 2025)

The report now covers August-October 2025 instead of just September-October.

### 3. Complete NVIDIA Driver Data
**Investigation:** The "N/A" values were appearing because NVIDIA driver changes are only documented in the "Nvidia Images" section of release changelogs. By examining the full release bodies from the GitHub API, I found the actual NVIDIA driver versions.

**Results:**
- **580.95.05-1** (Oct 11) - Latest NVIDIA driver
- **580.82.07-1** (Sep 3-Oct 2) - Maintained across 5 consecutive releases
- **580.76.05-1** (Aug 28-Sep 1) - Previous stable version

All releases now show actual NVIDIA driver versions with clear upgrade/stable indicators.

### 4. Enhanced Progression Tables
- **Kernel Version Progression:** Shows 8 releases with detailed change tracking including major version jump from 6.15.x to 6.16.x series
- **Mesa Driver Progression:** Complete history showing stability across 7 releases with one upgrade
- **NVIDIA Driver Progression:** New "Key Updates" section summarizes driver version lifecycles

### 5. Improved Documentation Clarity
- Updated all references from "last 5" to "last 8" releases
- Enhanced NVIDIA availability info box with clearer explanation of driver versioning across releases
- Added changelog entry documenting these updates
- Updated analysis period to reflect August-October 2025 timeframe

## Why These Changes Matter

1. **Faster troubleshooting:** Users can immediately copy/paste rebase commands without referring to separate documentation
2. **Better historical context:** 8 releases (~3 months) gives users more options when bisecting driver issues
3. **Complete NVIDIA data:** No more "N/A" values - users can see exactly which NVIDIA driver version each release contains
4. **Clear version tracking:** Every driver version is explicitly listed, even when unchanged, making it obvious which releases share the same drivers

## Testing

- ✅ Build passes successfully with `npm run build`
- ✅ All markdown syntax validated
- ✅ All GitHub links follow correct patterns
- ✅ Verified NVIDIA driver versions against actual GitHub release changelogs

author: jimmy058910
body:
## Summary

Consolidates 5 GitHub Actions workflows (418 lines) into 2 streamlined workflows (ci.yml + release.yml).

## Problem

- **5 separate workflows** with overlapping concerns and duplicate logic
- **Serial dependency:** Tests blocked by lint failures (one pre-commit violation blocks entire test matrix)
- **Frequent breakage:** Pre-commit hook drift causes CI failures after development
- **Duplication:** Pre-commit runs in both tests.yml and lint-full.yml
- **Complexity:** Docker builds spread across workflows

## Solution

### 1. **ci.yml** (replaces tests.yml, deps-compile-check.yml, lint-full.yml)

**Jobs:**
- `quick-checks` (2-3 min): actionlint, yamllint, deps-compile freshness, guardrails
- `test-matrix` (parallel, independent): Ubuntu/macOS × Python 3.10/3.11/3.12
  - No coverage on most legs
  - Coverage + Codecov upload on Ubuntu 3.11 only
- `lint-full` (nightly only): Full pre-commit suite (schedule trigger)

**Benefits:**
- Tests run immediately (no lint dependency blocking)
- Fast feedback loop
- Single source of truth for CI

### 2. **release.yml** (enhanced to absorb docker-build.yml)

**Jobs:**
- `pypi-publish`: Build/publish Python package to PyPI (Trusted Publishers OIDC)
- `docker-build`: Multi-arch builds (full/slim/alpine) after PyPI publish
- `docker-scan`: Trivy vulnerability scanning
- `docker-hub-readme`: README sync (placeholder for future)

**Benefits:**
- Consolidates release artifacts in one workflow
- Docker builds only run on version tags (saves CI time)
- Clear job dependencies (Docker builds after PyPI)

## Impact

- ✅ **60% reduction:** 5 → 2 workflows
- ✅ **Faster CI:** Parallel test matrix (no lint blocking)
- ✅ **Easier maintenance:** Single source of truth
- ✅ **Better UX:** Fewer GitHub Actions tabs, clearer status checks
- ✅ **ROADMAP-ready:** Simplified structure for future CI/CD features

## Migration Plan

1. ✅ Create new ci.yml + update release.yml
2. ⏳ **Test on this PR** (validate new workflows work)
3. ⏳ Delete deprecated workflows after green CI
4. ⏳ Update CLAUDE.md with new workflow references

## Testing

This PR will trigger the new `ci.yml` workflow. Expected results:

- ✅ `quick-checks` job passes (actionlint, yamllint, deps-compile)
- ✅ `test-matrix` job passes (6 configurations in parallel)
- ⏭️ `lint-full` job skipped (nightly only)

Old workflows (tests.yml, deps-compile-check.yml) will also run for comparison.

## Related

- Addresses user feedback: "After development, it always seems one or more [workflows] break"
- Prepares codebase for ROADMAP items #3–11 (CI/CD integration, policy-as-code, etc.)

---

author: kingpinxd
body:
# Description

Closes : https://github.com/zeta-chain/node/issues/4282

Success rate formula
Success Rate % = (Successful Votes + Transactions Added to Internal Tracker - Active Internal Trackers) / Block Scan Total × 100

Take actions / raise alerts when

1. The counter values for `inbound_votes_out_of_gas_errors_total` and `inbound_votes_posted_7m_gas_limit_total` dont match. Tese numbers should be similar , the vote is created instantly. We can use a threshold of 5

2. If the difference between `inbound_votes_block_scan_total` and `inbound_votes_posted_500k_gas_limit_total` exceeds a certain threshold. 
These number should ideally be equal. Accomdating some buffer we can use a threshold difference of 20.

3. If the difference between `inbound_votes_block_scan_total` and `inbound_votes_posted_7m_gas_limit_total` is exceeding a certain threshold
These number should at max be equal. Accommodating some buffer, we can use a threshold difference of 5.

4. If the difference between `inbound_votes_block_scan_total` and `inbound_votes_successful_total` exceeds a certain threshold.

5. If the value of `internal_trackers_active` exceeds a certain threshold
Ideally, this should be 0. During full network capacity, all cctxs might end up creating inbound trackers

4 and 5 are related; if the difference is high, the `internal_trackers_active` should be going up

Extreme conditions(Which are still okay) :
- The values for `inbound_votes_block_scan_total` , `inbound_votes_posted_500k_gas_limit_total` , `inbound_votes_posted_7m_gas_limit_total` match.
This means that the current node has beed executing all the cctxs. This is okayas long as this number is comparable to `inbound_votes_successful_total`. If its not, it would trigger alert `4`

- The value `inbound_votes_posted_7m_gas_limit_total` is 0 or very small. This means means that the node is not executing any cctxs.

# How Has This Been Tested?

<!--- Please describe the tests that you ran to verify your changes. Include instructions and any relevant details so others can reproduce. Link any optional github actions runs. -->

- [ ] Tested CCTX in localnet
- [ ] Tested in development environment
- [ ] Go unit tests
- [ ] Go integration tests
- [ ] Tested via GitHub Actions

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Introduce Prometheus metrics to track inbound voting via block-scan and trackers (incl. internal), wire them across Bitcoin/EVM/Solana/Sui/TON observers, and record out-of-gas/success outcomes and gas-limit usage.
> 
> - **Metrics (Prometheus)**:
>   - Add counters/gauges: `inbound_votes_block_scan_total`, `inbound_observations_tracker_total{internal}`, `inbound_votes_out_of_gas_errors_total`, `inbound_votes_posted_500k_gas_limit_total`, `inbound_votes_posted_7m_gas_limit_total`, `inbound_votes_successful_total`, `transactions_added_to_internal_tracker_total`, `internal_trackers_active`.
> - **Observers (wiring and API tweaks)**:
>   - **EVM**: increment metrics in block-scan paths (`ZetaSent`, ERC20 `Deposited`, Gateway `Deposited/Called/DepositedAndCalled`), tracker processing (v1/v2), and TSS-receive; extend functions to pass `isTracker`/`isInternal` flags; adjust tests accordingly.
>   - **Bitcoin**: increment block-scan and tracker observation metrics; rename `CheckReceiptForBtcTxHash` -> `CheckReceiptAndPostVoteForBtcTxHash`.
>   - **Solana**: increment metrics when voting from block-scan and trackers; extend `VoteInboundEvents` to accept `isTracker`/`isInternal`.
>   - **Sui**: increment metrics in event and tracker processing; propagate `isTracker`/`isInternal`.
>   - **TON**: increment metrics on inbound votes from block-scan and trackers; propagate flags.
>   - **Internal trackers**: update gauge on add/remove; count additions.
> - **ZetaCore client**:
>   - Track inbound vote results: increment out-of-gas and successful counters; count votes posted by gas limit tier.
> - **Tests**:

author: huzaif-nabi
body:
Closes #7153

---

### 🐛 The Problem

This PR fixes a regression introduced in `v1.12.2` that caused a `TypeError` when using the fetch adapter, particularly in environments like service workers.

If a request was made with a `config` object that did not have an `.env` property, the adapter would attempt to destructure an `undefined` value, causing the request to fail.

### 💡 The Solution

The fix ensures the `env` variable within the fetch adapter is always initialized as an object. It safely merges the `globalFetchAPI` with `config && config.env`, preventing the error and restoring the correct fallback behavior.

### ✅ Verification

The core Node.js test suite passes with this change. The fix has also been manually verified in the sandbox environment, confirming that basic requests no longer cause a crash.

author: clhain
body:
This change adds an action workflow to build a df_engine container and run a suite of 4 benchmark tests on each commit to main. Each test will run 100k log records per second through the engine, generated by the df_engine running the fake-signal receiver and received by the df_engine running a perf exporter. The test framework monitors cpu / memory / network utilization along with log sent/received/loss metrics. Each test runs either the OTAP or OTLP receiver, a simple attribute processor that renames a label, and either the OTAP or OTLP exporter. 

Additional "nightly" test suite(s) will be added to track other benchmarks (e.g. rx/tx formats, processors, signal types, batch sizes, etc) in followup PRs.

A followup PR will update the gh-actions-benchmark index.html page to support the data generated by these tests in our github pages site.
